references.text: Genesis 37:3 tells that Jacob gave Joseph a special coat (כְּתֹנֶת הַפַּסִּים), the same coat that his brothers strip from him in verse 23.
Genesis 37:28 continues the story by showing what happened after Joseph's brothers had stripped off his coat—they sold him to the Ishmaelites.
Genesis 37:31-32 describes what the brothers did with Joseph's coat after they took it from him—they dipped it in goat's blood and sent it to Jacob.
Acts 7:9 refers to Joseph's brothers who were jealous and sold him into Egypt, which is directly related to the event in Genesis 37:23.
Matthew 27:28 describes how the soldiers stripped Jesus and put a scarlet robe on him, a typological parallel to the stripping of Joseph.
Direct narrative connection where the tunic from 37:23 becomes the instrument of the lie in 37:31.
